items.summary: The Houthis said they carried out a new wave of attacks targeting two civilian airports — Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Najran Airport near the southern Saudi-Yemen border — plus the Royal Saudi Air Force's King Khalid Air Base, using cruise and ballistic missiles. Saudi authorities said three Saudi nationals were killed and several people of various nationalities injured across two attacks on the airport Thursday; falling missile debris damaged a kindergarten and a medical clinic. Houthi leader warned Saudi Arabia to prepare for a long conflict.
items.title: Oct 8: Houthi missile wave hits Riyadh airport, Najran airport and Saudi air base; 3 Saudis killed

items.summary: A Houthi missile struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, killing 13 people — four Saudis, two Bangladeshis, an American, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian, a Palestinian, a Sudanese, and later an Indian citizen who died of wounds — and wounding 309+. Security footage showed the terminal ceiling collapsing as passengers fled. Saudi Arabia's deadliest attack in more than a decade; the Saudi-led coalition called it a war crime.
items.title: Oct 10: Deadly Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport kills 13, wounds 300+

items.summary: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for the Oct 10 airport strike in a televised speech. The same day, an unidentified projectile hit Terminal 4 at King Khalid airport, killing one Pakistani resident, wounding 11 and starting a fire; Saudi air defenses intercepted a cruise missile nearby. Dammam's King Fahd International Airport also came under attack, and the Houthis claimed strikes on two Saudi Aramco facilities. Riyadh schools shifted to remote learning Sun–Thu; the US Mission issued security alerts for US citizens.
items.title: Oct 11: Houthis claim Riyadh strike; Terminal 4 hit (1 killed, 11 wounded), Dammam airport and Aramco sites targeted

items.summary: A fresh Houthi drone and cruise-missile wave targeted the kingdom's key oil and gas facilities; several were intercepted. King Khalid airport stays closed until at least Oct 17 (NOTAM) with 46% of flights cancelled across Saudi airports; the FAA warned US airlines on Saudi routes. The World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh was disrupted — the CEOs of ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, Shell and BP withdrew. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman vowed a serious retaliation.
items.title: Oct 12: Fresh Houthi wave targets Saudi oil/gas sites; Riyadh airport shut till Oct 17, energy summit disrupted

items.summary: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt and Saudi Arabia (the 'R4') jointly condemned the Houthi airport attacks as a 'dangerous escalation', backing all legitimate Saudi countermeasures and holding the Houthi militia fully accountable. The four signed a joint defence pact in August under which an attack on one is an attack on all; Turkey is assessing defensive/technical support for Riyadh but ruled out troop deployment and offensive operations.
items.title: Oct 12: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia jointly condemn attacks under defence pact
